card.question: Why do midterm elections often hurt the president's party?
card.answer: Voters often use midterms to register approval or frustration with the sitting president, and the president's party usually loses House and Senate seats as a result. Rising prices and a weak economy can make this effect stronger.

card.question: What is the difference between inclusive time and self time in a profiler?
card.answer: Inclusive time is the total time a function spends running, including every function it calls. Self time is only the time spent in the function's own code, not in anything it calls.

answer: Inclusive time counts everything a function takes including the functions it calls; self time counts just the function's own code.

card.question: Why does an LLM alone often miss performance problems in code it writes?
card.answer: An LLM checks syntax and local logic, so the code compiles and passes unit tests. It cannot see the runtime environment, the full call stack, or how often a function runs under production load, so waste only shows up at scale.

answer: The model only sees syntax and local logic, so the code runs and passes tests, but it has no view of the runtime, call stack or production frequency, so inefficiency only shows at scale.

card.question: Why does Netflix pair a stateless LLM with a Pattern Catalog?
card.answer: LLMs start every prompt with no memory of past bugs. The catalog is a shared store of known anti-patterns that gets injected into prompts, so one team's findings can help every other team and the same bug is not rediscovered repeatedly.

answer: LLMs forget everything between prompts, so a shared catalog of known anti-patterns is fed into prompts so teams share findings and don't rediscover the same bugs.

card.question: Why does Graham say consistent daily work matters more than bursts of effort?
card.answer: Work compounds. A small daily amount adds up over years, such as a page a day becoming a book a year. Early exponential growth looks flat, so people underrate it and quit before the curve takes off.

card.question: Why does a broken mental model make new ideas hard to see?

card.question: What is a remote access trojan (RAT)?
card.answer: A RAT is malware that lets an attacker take remote control of a victim's computer without the victim knowing. It works like legitimate remote-support software, but it runs silently and the attacker can see files, keystrokes, passwords, and the webcam.

answer: It's malware that gives an attacker secret remote control of a victim's machine, like remote-support software but silent, letting them see files, keystrokes, passwords and the webcam.
